question: On a large rendered page with a local action contract, what incremental verification value does the installed browser receipt SDK add to an already-strong directed host verifier?

comparison: H+R: the same directed host verifier plus one browser-SDK receipt cycle
excluded: whole-body accessibility snapshot as the baseline
personal Chrome, profiles, tabs, cookies, sessions, or extensions
external websites or external network requests

fixture.page: local deterministic HTML served on an operating-system-assigned loopback port other than 8377
fixture.largePage: 3000 decoy cards outside the operation scope
fixture.receiptRoot: the same local operation scope used by the directed verifier
actionContract: target status transitions from Ready to Approved
the operation scope contains no semantic evidence gap

cases.effect: target transitions; neighbor, actionability, and observability remain valid
target transitions but a new overlay intercepts its action control
target transitions but a new canvas in the operation scope contains an independently readable harmful pixel effect

schedule.readerOrder: balanced by (caseIndex + repetition) parity before and after the action

H.verdictPolicy: UNKNOWN if scope-observable is false; otherwise PASS iff every remaining predicate passes, else FAIL
H.evidence: JSON-safe observed facts and predicate results only

H+R.predicates: identical to H; no directed check may be removed
H+R.receipt: one pre-action baseline and one post-action receipt over the operation scope
H+R.verdictPolicy: the H verdict, except an additional receipt evidence gap or torn observation may conservatively yield UNKNOWN; the receipt may not manufacture PASS
H+R.evidence: the complete H evidence plus the SDK's public JSON-safe receipt

independentOracle.implementation: separate low-level DOM/pixel reader that does not call either arm or the SDK
independentOracle.passCondition: target Approved AND neighbor Ready AND centre-point hit target action AND no harmful canvas pixel
independentOracle.calibration: the oracle result must equal the preregistered truth for every trial or the experiment is INVALID

primaryMetrics.correctness: verdict equals oracle truth; UNKNOWN is not counted correct against PASS/FAIL truth
primaryMetrics.denominator: all 20 scheduled paired trials; operational errors remain in the denominator

secondaryMetrics.authoring: directed predicate count, host verification calls, and receipt API calls
secondaryMetrics.evidenceBytes: UTF-8 bytes of the exact JSON-safe arm evidence returned to the consumer
secondaryMetrics.runtimeIntegration: installed package fields, runtime dependency fields, bundle bytes/hash, and browser permission requirement
secondaryMetrics.wallTime: browser-side elapsed milliseconds, descriptive only; no speed superiority decision

integrityGates: the SDK is npm-packed and installed into a temporary directory with dev dependencies omitted
the installed SDK has no runtime dependency fields
Chromium uses a dedicated temporary persistent profile that is deleted
the loopback server chooses an OS-assigned port and rejects port 8377
all browser requests remain on the fixture origin or blob URLs
all 20 trials complete exactly once per arm
the independent oracle matches every preregistered truth
the runner, preregistration, tarball, installed bundle, and result receive SHA-256 provenance

decisionRule.incrementalCorrectness: supported only if H+R has fewer false greens or more correct verdicts without increasing false negatives, under the identical directed contract
decisionRule.incrementalDiagnosticOnly: if primary verdict metrics tie, any advantage must be described only as standardized evidence/uncertainty, with its byte, call, and wall-time costs
decisionRule.noDemonstratedIncrement: if metrics tie and receipt evidence does not add a uniquely consumable fact, report no incremental value for this fixed, well-authored contract
decisionRule.commercialClaim: no commercial-demand, willingness-to-pay, or multisite-generalization claim is estimable from this fixture
